query: Which material can be used for lightweight and superior comprehensive performance, and why?

generation.hypothesis: The AlCoCrFeNi 2.1 EHEA alloy exhibits superior comprehensive performance due to its homogeneous microstructure and balanced properties, which can be attributed to the eutectic design strategy utilizing physicochemical properties and CALPHAD thermodynamics calculations.
generation.intervention: Thermomechanical treatments, such as cold rolling
generation.mechanism: Eutectic design strategy and CALPHAD thermodynamics calculations
generation.predicted_outcome: Superior comprehensive performance, including high strength, ductility, and resistance to oxidation and corrosion
generation.boundary: Limited to the specific composition and processing conditions of the AlCoCrFeNi 2.1 EHEA alloy
generation.uncertainty: The exact mechanisms underlying the superior performance of the AlCoCrFeNi 2.1 EHEA alloy are not fully understood and require further investigation

falsification_experiment.design: Comparison of the comprehensive performance of the AlCoCrFeNi 2.1 EHEA alloy with traditional alloys of similar compositions
falsification_experiment.falsification_rule: If the AlCoCrFeNi 2.1 EHEA alloy does not exhibit superior comprehensive performance compared to traditional alloys, the hypothesis is falsified

cited_evidence.text: Mechanism with scope. Mechanism: Thermomechanical treatments (specifically cold rolling) can further tune mechanical properties by increasing proof and fracture stress while maintaining decent ductility through work hardening.. System: AlCoCrFeNi 2.1 EHEA. Conditions: Cold rolling with 8% thickness reduction; room temperature tensile testing. Evidence: measured. Observation: Cold rolling with 8% reduction increased the engineering proof stress to 275 MPa and fracture stress to 1145 MPa, while retaining 10.4% elongation.. Scope limits: The text notes this is a simple treatment; further optimization is needed for room-temperature and elevated temperature properties.. Alternatives: As-cast state properties which are already high but can be improved.. Quote: "The mechanical properties of the as-cast EHEA can be further tuned by thermomechanical treatments."

Mechanism with scope. Mechanism: The eutectic design strategy utilizes physicochemical properties (atomic radius, mixing enthalpy, valence electron concentration) and CALPHAD thermodynamics calculations to pinpoint eutectic compositions in multi-component systems.. System: General class of Eutectic High-Entropy Alloys (EHEAs). Conditions: Alloy design and thermodynamic calculation phase. Evidence: inferred. Observation: The authors successfully designed the AlCoCrFeNi 2.1 alloy using this strategy, resulting in a uniform microstructure and balanced properties.. Scope limits: Requires reliable thermodynamics databases for HEAs to be established; relies on the assumption of a pseudo-binary multi-component alloy system.. Alternatives: Traditional physical metallurgy principles which may not easily predict eutectic behavior in high-entropy systems.. Quote: "Further exploration of new EHEAs will be based on previous established physical metallurgy principles to design HEAs, utilizing physiochemical material properties including atomic radius, mixing enthalpy and valence electron concentration."
